rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this candidate raises obfuscation aggressiveness while keeping costs bounded for NPB dc's hot data-processing loops (MultiWayMerge, SharedSortAggregate, ComputeGivenGroupbys, PrefixedAggregate). SUB stays the backbone (highest weights, near-zero risk) since instruction substitution is cheap and always safe. FLA and BCF are pushed up to deepen control-flow flattening and bogus-edge coverage on the large aggregate/merge functions, with RuntimeCost weights held near mid-range so the scheduler still avoids applying them to the hottest inner loops. IBR is raised for block-order randomization to complement FLA's structure destruction, and SPLIT stays high since it is nearly free and increases basic-block fragmentation that other passes exploit. ICALL is kept at moderate weight with a slightly elevated CorrectnessRisk discount because indirect call rewriting touches the red-black tree and job-control call sites where function-pointer misuse would break the build; round 1's success justifies nudging it up but not to maximum. IGV remains lowest-weight: global-variable indirection gives modest security here (few hot globals beyond NPB timers) and carries tail-latency risk in the timed kernel loops. Overall the table biases toward diversity (all DiversityGain weights 0.6+) to maximize reverse-engineering resistance per the measured-clean round 1 baseline.
